input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Response.__init__ reads self.raw.reason to initialize reason, but raw has no underlying response object yet at construction time, so the attribute access dereferences None.
- failure path: Any call that builds a Response, such as every adapter.send or a plain Response(), raises AttributeError ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'reason') before the object is populated, so no request can complete.

Reviewer finding
- description: Response.__init__ now sets self.reason from self.raw.reason, but self.raw has no value at this point in construction, so instantiating Response() raises an AttributeError.
- rationale: Trigger: any code calling Response() with no arguments, such as a test or a custom adapter that builds an empty Response before filling it in. Mechanism: line 793 evaluates self.raw.reason while self.raw is unset or None, which raises before the constructor finishes. Impact: the constructor crashes on a path that previously worked, so callers that create a bare Response get an exception instead of an object.
critique: The finding describes the same defect: Response.__init__ reads self.raw.reason while raw is still None/unset during construction, so it raises AttributeError. The only difference is that the finding stresses bare Response() calls, while the label also covers adapter.send. The faulty operation and mechanism are identical.
